result.recommended_anchor: backend/autoresearch/strategy_backtest_adapter.py:167 `make_engine_backtest_fn`. It is the ONLY sweep-level PBO producer that is (a) library code rather than a one-shot script, so a criterion written against it stays true; (b) on a path that actually reaches PromotionGate.evaluate (rotation_runner.py:271/:278 -> strategy_candidate_producer.py:148 -> strategy_selector.py:94); (c) already emitting the 82.23 provenance fields (:264-278); and (d) enforcing Bailey Algorithm 2.3's same-model-different-configuration rule at :94-108 with a hard ValueError on an unknown strategy so the engine cannot silently fall back to triple_barrier. scripts/harness/run_82_3_candidate_backtests.py:143 is a genuine second sweep producer but is a one-shot evidence script that never calls the gate -- name it as the OFFLINE evidence producer, not the anchor. quant_optimizer.py is disqualified twice over: it retains no per-iteration return series (only scalars, :610) and it is a guided search, whose intermediate steps Bailey Sec 5.2 explicitly forbids as CSCV columns.
key_findings: Q1 SETTLED verbatim from the paper (read in full, 34pp via curl+pdfplumber, https://www.davidhbailey.com/dhbpapers/backtest-prob.pdf): Algorithm 2.3 -- 'each column n = 1,...,N represents a vector of profits and losses over t = 1,...,T observations associated with a particular model configuration tried by the researcher. M is therefore a real-valued matrix of order (T x N)', with conditions (i) synchronous rows across the N trials and (ii) the metric estimable on subsamples; 'If different model configurations trade with different frequencies, observations should be aggregated to match a common index'.

Guided-search exclusion is EXPLICIT (paper Sec 5.2): 'the columns of matrix M should be the final outcome of each guided search (i.e., after it has converged to a solution), and not the intermediate steps.' This disqualifies backend/backtest/quant_optimizer.py:302 as a column source independently of its lack of series retention.

Requirements on N and T, verbatim: 'if the investor is sensitive to values of phi < 1/10 ... N >> 10 is required'; 'T should be chosen to be double of the number of observations used by the investor to choose a model configuration'. S=16 is justified as producing 12,780 logits with sigma[f(lambda)] < 0.0045 on ~4 years of daily data.

Q2 -- UNANIMOUS architectural convention across every implementation found: the (T x N) matrix is owned by the object that RAN THE SWEEP. CRAN `pbo` takes a user-assembled data frame and its own example uses N <- 200 (https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/pbo/readme/README.html); the reference Python walk-through builds `R_mat = pd.DataFrame(R).T  # shape: (n_configs, n_combinations)` AFTER the sweeps complete; mlfinlab's cross_validation/combinatorial.py generates N backtest paths but does NOT compute PBO at all (statistics live in a separate module). No implementation computes PBO inside a single-run report object -- external corroboration that 82.23's criterion was unsatisfiable.

Q3 -- 'return 0.0 on N<2' is NOT a documented trap anywhere. CRAN pbo, mlfinlab and the reference Python implementation ALL document zero small-N behaviour; the paper gives only a magnitude rule (N >> 10), not a branch. So backend/backtest/analytics.py:297-298 is a pyfinagent-LOCAL invention, and the chosen sentinel is the best possible value on a ceiling gate. Do not cite a precedent that does not exist.

MEASURED WIRING DEFECT (the highest-value finding): the adapter's `pbo` DOES reach PromotionGate.evaluate, but `pbo_n_trials` does NOT. backend/autoresearch/strategy_candidate_producer.py:115-123 rebuilds the candidate from a hardcoded 5-key whitelist (strategy, dsr, pbo, params, sharpe), discarding pbo_n_trials/pbo_n_obs/pbo_gate_grade/pbo_column_corr_mean/pbo_columns_diverse. Ran live against the real modules: with pbo_n_trials=3 the gate returns {'promoted': True}; with the key restored it returns {'promoted': False, 'reason': 'pbo_trials_below_min:3<10'}. The 82.23 min_pbo_trials=10 floor (gate.py:43-53) is therefore DEAD on the only live producer path, and _DEFAULT_K=8 (adapter :70) sits below it. 82.27 NEEDS A WIRING CHANGE, not only tests.

Hop trace for I4: scripts/run_rotation_smoke.py:58 -> rotation_runner.run_rotation_bakeoff:241 -> make_engine_backtest_fn (:271) -> run_strategy_bakeoff (:278) -> strategy_candidate_producer.py:148 build_per_strategy_candidates -> strategy_selector.py:150 select_best_strategy -> g.evaluate(c) at strategy_selector.py:94. Real and closed -- but NOTHING SCHEDULES IT: rotation_runner.py:36 and strategy_candidate_producer.py:33 both still list 'The weekly rotation CRON' as DEFERRED, and no rotation scheduling exists in backend/services, backend/main.py or backend/slack_bot.

I3 -- backend/agents/mcp_servers/risk_server.py:133-158 is a CONSUMER, not a third producer: `pnl_matrix` arrives as a tool ARGUMENT; the server never assembles a matrix or runs a backtest. It does re-expose the false-good, however, because it calls raw compute_pbo at :142-143 -- a one-line swap to compute_pbo_checked. Consumer fix, optional for 82.27; must not be described as a producer.

I5 -- backend/backtest/experiments/quant_results.tsv has NO pbo column (header: timestamp run_id param_changed metric_before metric_after delta status dsr top5_mda params_json parent_run_id; 539 rows). The 7 'pbo' matches are inside the params_json blob on rows 533-539 only (the 82.3-passA/passB rows). Of 437 files in backend/backtest/experiments/results/, exactly 3 contain a "pbo" key -- all phase-82.3 outputs (20260803T175308Z_phase_82_3_candidate_comparison.json, 20260804T025319Z_phase_82_3_full_sample_3strat.json, 20260804T041628Z_phase_82_3_short_window_4strat.json).

Literature backing for the existing columns_diverse field: the paper's own Sec 5.2 limitation 4 states 'it is entirely possible that all the N strategies have high but similar Sharpe ratios. Since none of the strategies is clearly better than the rest, PBO will be high.' The measured 82.3 column correlation of 0.967-0.979 puts the incumbent's 0.7486 squarely in that documented benign regime -- report it as 'not gate-grade evidence', NOT as 'the incumbent is overfit'.

Paper also forbids PBO as an optimisation objective (Sec 5.2 limitation 5, citing Strathern): 'CSCV can be employed to evaluate the quality of a strategy selection process, but PBO should not be the objective function on which such selection relies.' Keep PBO out of quant_optimizer's search objective; the promotion gate is the correct home.

Recency scan (2024-2026) performed with three query variants: 2 relevant findings, NEITHER supersedes CSCV. (1) Arian, Norouzi M. & Seco (2024), Knowledge-Based Systems S0950705124011110 / SSRN 4778909 -- CPCV beats K-Fold/Purged K-Fold/Walk-Forward, MEASURED BY lower PBO and higher DSR, plus new Bagged/Adaptive CPCV variants; it changes how columns are GENERATED, not what they are or who owns them. (2) arXiv:2512.12924v1 (Dec 2025, read in full) -- cites CSCV as the reference method and Arian 2024, notes 'walk-forward remains the industry standard', and explicitly declines to apply deflation to its own results. No 2026 work on PBO/CSCV surfaced.

File-drawer pitfall now mapped to code: backend/autoresearch/strategy_backtest_adapter.py:212-216 silently DROPS a failed variant's column. The paper warns 'Hiding trials will lead to an underestimation of the overfit' -- systematically dropping losers biases PBO DOWN. Worth emitting a dropped-column count alongside pbo.
